questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The proximity of Italy's art history. Studying history, I see no better place than Bologna. I wanted to be at the physical location of the subject matter in my studies.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: A little difficult, but I survived through communication with other Erasmus-students who were equally confused.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
Not much. You were left to yourself in terms of finding accommodation in which Bologna is absolutely impossible. I spent the first month from September 3rd to October 15th on looking for a place to sleep. 
The initial assistance was a video-check in with a few informations on how to operate the IT-systems. They helped.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: impossible.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: They should go to Bologna at least three months before their stay, physically, to be sure not to get scammed, and then find housing. There are a lot of frauds in Bologna. They must see the places themselves.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I'm never good at bureaucracy, and this was no exception.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Online check in with proof of flight ticket. Firstly you had to register online at AlmaRM and you had to fill out a study plan in accordance to your pre approved courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: A supporting e-mail for incoming students on the faculty of humanities. They replied quickly.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Completely succesful after a few tries.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ask other incoming exchange students and write the mobility assistance e-mail.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Absolutely amazing.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The art history of medieval and early modern art was of such high level, that I am now crucially inspired to learn everything about those subjects. Absolutely high level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Way less Foucault and meta-talk that the North in their perpetual americanization has become so fond of. Instead, In Italy you approach the subjects more in the "ad fontes"-way, where you go directly to the source material of history and do not spend most of the time making methodological discussions. In some courses the teaching was a bit more relaxed and easy to process than in UCPH, but it highly depends on which course we are talking.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Early modern art
history medieval and early renaissance art
a survey of early modern italian and European architecture
history of Italian cinema
rome and the universal

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sport facilities out of town with tennis and swimming. Concerts and parties.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Travel around at see the beauty of northern Italy. Go to concerts. I was annoyed by all the Erasmus-events because it felt like a summer camp for mindless cattle, but I think people in general liked them.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: See the Pinacoteca, the tomb of San Domenico, go to Modena, Parma, Firenze, Rome and see all of Italy's art!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy and nice. I tried to learn a bit of Italian and understand a fair amount now. The culture is more relaxed and pleasant than that of Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to bars, smile, and talk.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The social usage of the city, the food, the coffee, the aperitivi.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Get your housing well in advance, and be very careful of scammers!
appreciate the rich history of the area.
Stay hydrated. They eat a lot of salt.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The beauty of art in Italy, the learning of 2000-years' art history and falling in love with an italian woman.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The initial housing problem.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Enjoy. It's a wonderful life if we can find it.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
